title: Around town
cando: ask for and follow directions, and understand signs in town

about.text: In this lesson you are out in town. You ask the way, follow directions and read signs. At the end, you tell a visitor the way to your home.
goals: Ask the way: Could you tell me the way to the museum?
Give directions: Go straight on. Turn left. Go past the cinema.
Say where a place is: It's opposite the park.
Read a “How to find us” notice and a “Bridge closed” sign.
Tell a visitor the way from the station to your home.

chapters.title: Asking the way
chapters.text:
In this lesson you are out in town. You need to find a place.
First, you listen to Samir. He has a job interview at the museum. But he doesn't know the way.
He stops a woman in the street. He says: Excuse me. Could you tell me the way to the museum, please?
Could you is very polite. It is good with people you don't know.
Listen to Samir. He asks the woman to say it again. Then he says the directions back.
This is a good habit. It helps you remember the way.

chapters.title: Directions and places
chapters.text:
Directions start with a verb. Go straight on. Turn left. Go past the cinema. Cross the bridge.
Turn left tells you where to go. On the left tells you where the place is.
Turn left at the bank. The café is on the left.
At the end, say where the place is. Use opposite, between, in front of or behind.
The museum is opposite the park. The post office is between the bank and the café.
Do not say opposite of. Say: opposite the park. But say: in front of the cinema.

chapters.title: A notice and a sign
chapters.text:
Next, you read a notice. Its title is How to find us.
It tells visitors the way from the station to a community centre.
On the way, there is a sign on a bridge. The bridge is closed, so you need a new way.
Read the dates and the numbers slowly. They are important.
Then you write directions from the station to your home. Write one step on each line.

chapters.title: Guiding a visitor
chapters.text:
In the task, a colleague is coming to your home. She is at the station, and she phones you.
Tell her the way, one step at a time. Name things she can see: the traffic lights, a supermarket, a park.
Then you change roles. Your teacher gives you directions to a new place. Say them back to check.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about finding the way in a town.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You are in a new town. You can't find a place. What do you do?
choices: look at a map on my phone
go into a shop and ask
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people look at a map on their phone. But asking a person is often quicker. And it is good English practice.

conversation.title: The way to the museum
conversation.setting: Samir has a job interview at the museum at ten o'clock. He comes out of the station. The map on his phone doesn't help, so he asks a woman.
lines: Excuse me. Could you tell me the way to the museum, please?
Yes, of course. Go straight on to the traffic lights.
Straight on to the traffic lights.
Turn left at the traffic lights. Then cross the bridge.
Sorry, can you say that again, please?
Turn left at the traffic lights, and cross the bridge.
Left at the lights, and cross the bridge. OK.
Go past the post office and the cinema.
Past the post office and the cinema.
The museum is on the corner. It's opposite the park.
Opposite the park. Is it far? My interview is at ten.
No, it's about ten minutes on foot. Good luck!

questions.q: Where does Samir want to go?
questions.why: Samir asks: Could you tell me the way to the museum?

questions.q: What does Samir do at the traffic lights?
questions.why: The woman says: Turn left at the traffic lights.

questions.a: on the corner, opposite the park
questions.why: The woman says: The museum is on the corner. It's opposite the park.

phrases.text: Excuse me. Could you tell me the way to the museum?
Go straight on to the traffic lights.
Turn left at the traffic lights.

phrases.use: Saying what you walk by on the way.

phrases.text: Sorry, can you say that again, please?
phrases.use: When the directions are too fast.

phrases.text: Left at the lights, and cross the bridge.
phrases.use: Saying the directions back, to check them.

items.meaning: To change the way you are going: left or right.
items.example: Turn left at the bank.

items.meaning: To walk or drive by a place, and not stop.
items.example: Go past the supermarket and turn right.

items.meaning: To go from one side of a road to the other.
items.example: Cross the road at the traffic lights.

items.meaning: On the other side of the road or the room.
items.example: The bank is opposite the station.

items.meaning: The place where two streets meet.
items.example: The café is on the corner.

items.meaning: They tell cars when to stop and go. Red is stop, and green is go.
items.example: Turn left at the traffic lights.

items.meaning: You walk or drive over it, above a river or a road.
items.example: Cross the bridge and turn right.

items.meaning: A picture of a town or a country, with the roads and places.
items.example: I looked at the map on my phone.

items.meaning: A place where you send letters and parcels, and buy stamps.
items.example: I need to send this parcel. Is there a post office near here?

items.meaning: A place where you watch films on a big screen.
items.example: There's a new film at the cinema this week.

items.meaning: A small place where you can buy coffee, tea and something to eat.
items.example: Let's meet at the café opposite the station.

items.meaning: A big shop that sells food and things for the home.
items.example: I buy my food at the supermarket after work.

items.meaning: A building where you can look at old or important things.
items.example: The museum is free on Sundays.

items.meaning: A big green place in a town. People walk and sit there.
items.example: I walk in the park at lunchtime.

sound.title: straight, cross, bridge
sound.explain: These words start with two or three sounds together. Say them together. Do not add a sound before them or between them. Straight is one part, not two. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Samir's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Do you sound polite and clear?
lines: Excuse me. Could you tell me the way to the museum, please?
Sorry, can you say that again, please?
Left at the lights, and cross the bridge. OK.
Opposite the park. Is it far? My interview is at ten.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Three tell Samir where to go. One tells him where the museum is.
examples: Go straight on to the traffic lights.
Turn left at the traffic lights.
Go past the post office and the cinema.
spot.question: How do the first three sentences start? Which sentence tells you where the museum is?
spot.answer: The first three start with a verb: go, turn, go past. Directions do this. It's opposite the park tells you where the museum is. There is no of after opposite.

rules.title: Directions: go, turn, cross, go past
rule: Start with a verb: Go straight on. Turn left. Turn right.
Say where: Turn left at the traffic lights. Turn right at the corner.
Go past the cinema. Cross the road. Cross the bridge.
At the end, say where it is: It's on the left. It's on the right.
Turn left: you go that way. On the left: the place is there.
rules.mistake: Not: Turn on the left at the bank. Say: Turn left at the bank.

rules.title: Where is it? opposite, between, in front of, behind
rule: opposite: The café is opposite the park. The road is between them.
between: The post office is between the bank and the café.
in front of: The bus stop is in front of the cinema.
behind: The car park is behind the supermarket.
No of after opposite. But in front of has of.
rules.mistake: Not: It's opposite of the bank. Say: It's opposite the bank.

practice.q: ___ straight on to the traffic lights.
practice.why: Directions start with the verb: Go straight on.
Turn left: you go that way. No on and no the.
On the left says where the place is.

practice.q: Don't turn. Go ___ the cinema, and then turn right.
practice.why: Go past: you walk by it, and you do not stop.

practice.q: The post office is ___ the bank and the café.
practice.why: Between goes with two places: the bank and the café.

practice.q: The bus stop is in front ___ the cinema.
practice.why: In front of is three words: in, front, of.
No of after opposite: opposite the park.

practice.q: ___ the road at the traffic lights. Wait for the green light.
practice.why: Cross: go from one side of the road to the other.

practice.q: My car is ___ the building. You can't see it from the street.
practice.why: Behind: at the back, so you can't see it from the street.

practice.q: Go past the park and ___ right.
practice.why: Directions use the verb with no -s and no -ing: turn right.

yourTurn.prompt: Think of a street near your home or your work. Write four sentences about where things are. Use opposite, between, in front of and behind.
starters: There is a … in front of …
yourTurn.model: The supermarket is opposite the station. The post office is between the bank and a small café. There is a bus stop in front of the post office. The car park is behind the supermarket.

text.title: How to find us, and a sign
text.body:
PRACTICE NOTICE: this centre does not exist.

HOW TO FIND US
Ashgrove Community Centre, 12 River Road
From the station: about 10 minutes on foot

1. Come out of the station and turn right.
2. Walk to the traffic lights and cross the road.
3. Go past the supermarket. Turn left at the corner.
4. Cross the bridge over the river.
5. We are at the end of River Road, opposite the park.
6. We are in a big white building. The entrance is at the back, behind the trees.

Lost? Phone us on 01632 960 418.

- - - - - - - -

BRIDGE CLOSED
3 to 14 June: this bridge is closed for work.
Walking to River Road? Turn right.
Walk 300 metres along the river to the next bridge.
It is next to the museum.
Cross it, then turn left.
Cars: please use Mill Road.

gist.q: What does the notice tell you?
gist.a: the way from the station to the centre
gist.why: The notice gives directions from the station: about 10 minutes on foot.

gist.q: Why is there a sign on the bridge?
gist.a: The bridge is closed for work.
gist.why: The sign says: this bridge is closed for work.

detail.a: at the end of River Road, opposite the park
detail.why: Step 5: We are at the end of River Road, opposite the park.

detail.a: at the back, behind the trees
wrong: at the front, on River Road
detail.why: Step 6 says: The entrance is at the back, behind the trees.

detail.q: It is 10 June. You are walking to the centre. What does the sign tell you to do?
detail.a: walk to the next bridge and cross there
detail.why: The bridge is closed from 3 to 14 June. People walking cross at the next bridge.

detail.q: How far is it to the next bridge?
detail.why: The sign says: Walk 300 metres along the river to the next bridge.

items.meaning: The door or the way into a building.
items.example: The entrance is at the back of the building.

items.meaning: A place with walls and a roof, like a house or an office.
items.example: Our office is on the second floor of a tall building.

items.meaning: The middle part of a town. Or a building for classes, sport or meetings.
items.example: Our new office is in the town centre.

items.meaning: To go on foot, not by bus or by car.
items.example: I walk to work. It takes 15 minutes.

items.meaning: We say how far a place is in these. A big step is about one.
items.example: The bus stop is 200 metres from here.

items.meaning: The last part of something, like a road or a film.
items.example: The post office is at the end of the street.

items.meaning: A long line of water that goes to the sea.
items.example: We walked along the river after work.

items.meaning: A very big, tall plant. Many grow in parks and forests.
items.example: There are tall trees in front of our building.

model.title: Directions to my home
model.body:
From the station to my home
1. Come out of the station and turn left.
2. Go straight on to the traffic lights.
3. Cross the road and go past the supermarket.
4. Turn right at the corner. That's Hill Street.
5. My building is number 24. It's opposite the park, next to a small café.
It's about ten minutes on foot.

write.task: Write directions from the station, or a bus stop, to your home. It can be a real home or a made-up one. Write one step on each line, like the model.
write.starter: 1. Come out of the station and …
checklist: I started each step with a verb: go, turn, cross.
I named things a visitor can see: traffic lights, a shop, a park.
At the end, I said where my home is: opposite, next to, between …
I wrote one step on each line.

card.title: Guide a visitor
card.situation: Your new colleague Lena is coming to your home for dinner on Saturday. She is at the station. She doesn't know the way, so she phones you.
card.goal: Tell Lena the way to your home, one step at a time. Then change roles: listen to directions to a new place, and say them back.

phrases: Come out of the station and turn left.
Go straight on to the traffic lights.
Go past the supermarket and cross the road.
My building is opposite the park.
Could you tell me the way to the museum?
So, right at the corner, then past the café?
prepare.notes: Draw a small map from the station to your home. Write the steps. Add one thing near your home that your visitor can see.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is Lena at the station. Tell her the way to your home. Then your teacher gives you directions to a new place. Say them back to check.
doIt.wehel: You are my new colleague, Lena. You are at the station in my town, and you are coming to my home for dinner. Phone me and ask the way. Say my directions back to check them. Then give me directions from the station to a café. Use simple English.

model.title: The call from the station
lines: Hi, it's Lena. I'm at the station. How do I get to your flat?
Hi, Lena! It's easy. Come out of the station and turn left.
Go straight on to the traffic lights. Then cross the road.
Straight on to the traffic lights, and cross the road.
Yes. Go past the supermarket. Then turn right at the corner. That's Hill Street.
Past the supermarket, and right at the corner. Then?
My building is number 24. It's opposite the park, next to a small café.
Number 24, opposite the park. Is it far?
No. It's about ten minutes on foot.
compare: Did you give the steps in order, one at a time?
Did you name things Lena can see: traffic lights, a supermarket, a park?
Did you say where your home is at the end?
When you listened to directions, did you say them back?

canDo: I can ask the way to a place in town.
I can understand and follow simple directions.
I can say where a place is: opposite, between, in front of, behind.
I can read a “How to find us” notice and a street sign.
I can tell a visitor the way to my home.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. Where is the person? Where do you think they want to go?
reading.talk: Is it easy to find places in your town? What helps you: a map, a sign or a person? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: Excuse me. Could you tell me the ___ to the station?
quiz.why: Could you tell me the way to …? asks for directions.

quiz.q: The museum is ___ the left, next to the bank.
quiz.why: On the left says where a place is.

quiz.q: The café is on one side of the road. The park is on the other side. The café is ___ the park.
quiz.why: Opposite: on the other side of the road.

quiz.q: Wait for me in ___ of the cinema.
quiz.why: In front of is three words: in, front, of.

quiz.q: They tell cars when to stop and go. What are they?
quiz.why: Red means stop, and green means go.

quiz.q: A sign says: BRIDGE CLOSED. What do you do?
quiz.why: The bridge is closed, so you need a new way.

quiz.q: The directions are very fast. What can you say?
options: Sorry, can you say that again, please?
quiz.a: Sorry, can you say that again, please?
quiz.why: Ask the person to say it again. It is polite, and it is normal.
You can't count rice, so some.

quiz.q: I've got a bad cough. — You ___ drink hot water with honey.
quiz.why: Should + a verb, with no to.

quiz.q: These shoes are ___ small. Have you got a bigger size?
quiz.why: Too small: smaller than you need.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the museum conversation in pairs. Then change the place: the post office, the cinema, a supermarket. The listener always says the directions back.
Day 2: map game. Draw a simple street on the board. Learners say where places are with opposite, between, in front of and behind, and the others add them to the map.
Day 3: the task. You are Lena at the station; each learner guides you to their home. Then give each learner directions to a new place, and they say them back.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and read two learners' directions aloud. The class follows them on a map.
